# Public API Reference (Byz_*)

TinyBFT exposes a libbyz-compatible C interface through the single header
`include/esp-tinybft.h`. The header declares buffer types, three callback
signatures, a client API, and a replica API. There is exactly one
replica and one client per process; the implementation keeps file-static
pointers (`s_replica`, `s_client`, `s_is_replica` in
`src/tbft_libbyz.c:41-43`) that are assigned by the `Byz_init_*` family
and dereferenced by every subsequent call.

## Overview

The contract:

- A single FreeRTOS task calls `Byz_init_replica` (replica role) or
  `Byz_init_client` (client role) once, then enters the run loop.
- Application state is owned by the caller; TinyBFT treats the buffer as
  opaque bytes and computes SHA-256 digests over each
  `TBFT_BLOCK_SIZE` chunk.
- Authentication is HMAC-SHA256 for hot-path messages and RSA-2048
  signatures for slow-path messages. The transport layer (UDP or
  ESP-NOW, selected at compile time) is invisible to the API.

The full list of public symbols, grouped by category, is below.

## Buffer types

Declared in `include/esp-tinybft.h:83-99`.

### `Byz_req`

```c
typedef struct {
    char *contents;
    int   size;
} Byz_req;
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `contents` | Command payload. Allocated by `Byz_alloc_request` (heap); freed by `Byz_free_request`. The first 68 bytes are the `tbft_request_rep_t` header that the BFT layer prepends to every client request — the application payload follows. |
| `size` | Size of the payload in bytes. Set by the application before calling `Byz_send_request` / `Byz_invoke` / `Byz_invoke_with_retry`. |

### `Byz_rep`

```c
typedef struct {
    char *contents;
    int   size;
} Byz_rep;
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `contents` | Reply payload. Allocated by the library inside `Byz_recv_reply` (or by `Byz_invoke`); freed by `Byz_free_reply`. |
| `size` | Size of the reply payload in bytes, capped at `TBFT_MAX_REPLY_SIZE`. |

### `Byz_buffer`

```c
typedef struct {
    char *contents;
    int   size;
} Byz_buffer;
```

Generic byte buffer used for non-deterministic choices. The size of
`contents` is `TBFT_NDET_BUF_SIZE` when passed to `Byz_init_replica` via
`ndet_max_len`.

## Callback types

Declared in `include/esp-tinybft.h:105-133`.

### `Byz_exec_cb`

```c
typedef int (*Byz_exec_cb)(Byz_req *in, Byz_rep *out, Byz_buffer *ndet,
                           int cid, bool ro);
```

Execute callback. Invoked by the library when a request is committed
and ready to execute. The callback runs in the replica's task context.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `in` | Committed request payload. The first 68 bytes are the BFT-layer header; the application command follows. `in->size` is the total length including header. |
| `out` | Buffer to write the reply into. The callback sets `out->size` to the number of bytes written. |
| `ndet` | Non-deterministic choices buffer. May be NULL if the application does not register a comp_ndet callback. |
| `cid` | Client id of the requester. |
| `ro` | True if this is a read-only request (skips `Byz_modify` requirements). |

**Return value:** `0` on success (reply is sent to the client), `-1` to
reject (no reply sent).

### `Byz_comp_ndet_cb`

```c
typedef void (*Byz_comp_ndet_cb)(int64_t seqno, Byz_buffer *ndet, int max_len);
```

Compute non-deterministic choices. Invoked by the primary when assigning
a sequence number to a new request batch.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `seqno` | Sequence number being ordered. |
| `ndet` | Buffer to fill. |
| `max_len` | Maximum bytes the library will accept (`ndet_max_len` from `Byz_init_replica`). |

### `Byz_recv_reply_cb`

```c
typedef void (*Byz_recv_reply_cb)(Byz_rep *reply, int cid);
```

Reply notification callback. Invoked by the library when it is about
to send a reply to client `cid`. May be NULL.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `reply` | The reply buffer the library is about to send. |
| `cid` | Destination client id. |

## Client API

### `Byz_init_client`

```c
int Byz_init_client(const char *config_file, const char *priv_config,
                    int local_id, uint16_t port);
```

Defined in `include/esp-tinybft.h:150-151`, implemented in
`src/tbft_libbyz.c:476`.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `config_file` | Path to the cluster configuration file (SPIFFS, e.g. `/spiffs/config_espnow.txt`). |
| `priv_config` | Path to the private key DER file (e.g. `/spiffs/priv7.der`). |
| `local_id` | Node slot this client occupies in the config (must be in `[num_replicas, num_nodes-1]`). Pass `-1` to auto-select the first client slot (3f+1). |
| `port` | UDP port to bind (0 = OS-assigned). Ignored for ESP-NOW. |

**Return value:** `0` on success, `-1` on error (file open, key parse,
allocation failure, etc.).

### `Byz_alloc_request`

```c
int Byz_alloc_request(Byz_req *req, int size);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:160`.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `req` | Output. `req->contents` is heap-allocated with `size` bytes. |
| `size` | Payload size in bytes (caller-fills the buffer, then sets `req->size`). |

**Return value:** `0` on success, `-1` on allocation failure.

### `Byz_send_request`

```c
int Byz_send_request(Byz_req *req, bool read_only);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:169`.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `req` | Populated request buffer (see `Byz_alloc_request`). |
| `read_only` | True if the request is read-only (no state modification). |

**Return value:** `0` on success, `-1` on error.

### `Byz_recv_reply`

```c
int Byz_recv_reply(Byz_rep *rep);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:177`. Blocks until `f+1` matching replies are
collected from distinct replicas.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `rep` | Output. `rep->contents` is heap-allocated by the library. |

**Return value:** `0` on success, `-1` on timeout or mismatch.

### `Byz_invoke`

```c
int Byz_invoke(Byz_req *req, Byz_rep *rep, bool read_only);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:184`. Convenience wrapper around
`Byz_send_request` + `Byz_recv_reply`.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `req` | Populated request buffer. |
| `rep` | Output. |
| `read_only` | True if the request is read-only. |

**Return value:** `0` on success, `-1` on error.

### `Byz_invoke_with_retry`

```c
int Byz_invoke_with_retry(Byz_req *req, Byz_rep *rep, bool read_only,
                          int max_attempts);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:209-210`. Sends a request and waits for a reply,
with bounded retry and exponential backoff. Each attempt calls
`Byz_invoke()`, which has its own per-attempt timeout of
`TBFT_CLIENT_REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 10 s for `simple_wallet`, 20 s
for `counter`). On timeout, the call sleeps for `delay_ms` (doubling
each attempt, capped at 10 s) and retries until `max_attempts` is
reached.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `req` | Populated request buffer. Must remain valid for the duration of the call. The underlying transport increments `rid` per attempt, so retries are treated as fresh consensus operations. |
| `rep` | Output. |
| `read_only` | True if the request is read-only. |
| `max_attempts` | Maximum number of attempts (must be >= 1). Use a small value (e.g. 3) for non-idempotent requests and a larger value (e.g. 8) for idempotent ones. |

**Return value:** Number of attempts used on success (1..max_attempts),
or `-1` if all attempts timed out or errored.

### `Byz_free_request`

```c
void Byz_free_request(Byz_req *req);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:213`. Frees `req->contents` (heap-allocated by
`Byz_alloc_request`).

### `Byz_free_reply`

```c
void Byz_free_reply(Byz_rep *rep);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:216`. Frees `rep->contents` (heap-allocated by
`Byz_recv_reply` or `Byz_invoke`).

### `Byz_reset_client`

```c
void Byz_reset_client(void);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:219`. Resets all pending requests and client state.

## Replica API

### `Byz_init_replica`

```c
int Byz_init_replica(const char *config_file, const char *priv_config,
                     int local_id,
                     void *mem, size_t mem_size,
                     Byz_exec_cb exec_cb,
                     Byz_comp_ndet_cb comp_ndet_cb, int ndet_max_len,
                     Byz_recv_reply_cb recv_reply_cb,
                     uint16_t port);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:245-251`, implemented in `src/tbft_libbyz.c:874`.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `config_file` | Path to the cluster configuration file. |
| `priv_config` | Path to the private key DER file. |
| `local_id` | Replica slot this board occupies (0..3f). Must match the node entry in `config_file` whose `priv_config` corresponds to; otherwise peers will reject this replica's authenticators. Pass `-1` to auto-detect from the local WiFi MAC (ESP-NOW only; WiFi must be started first). |
| `mem` | Application state buffer (must remain valid for the lifetime of the replica). |
| `mem_size` | State buffer size (multiple of `TBFT_BLOCK_SIZE`). |
| `exec_cb` | Execution callback. Must not be NULL. |
| `comp_ndet_cb` | Non-deterministic choices callback. May be NULL. |
| `ndet_max_len` | Max bytes for non-deterministic choices. |
| `recv_reply_cb` | Reply notification callback. May be NULL. |
| `port` | UDP port (0 = from config file). Ignored for ESP-NOW. |

**Return value:** `0` on success, `-1` on error. On success, a
`tbft_replica_t` is heap-allocated and stored in the file-static
`s_replica` pointer (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:41`).

### `Byz_modify`

```c
void Byz_modify(void *mem, int size);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:260`. Notify the library that the region
`[mem, mem+size)` of application state is about to be modified. Must be
called before any write to state.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `mem` | Pointer within the state buffer. |
| `size` | Number of bytes to be modified. |

### `Byz_modify1`

```c
void Byz_modify1(void *mem);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:266`. Convenience wrapper: notifies the library
that a single state block containing `mem` is about to be modified.

### `Byz_replica_run`

```c
void Byz_replica_run(void);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:272`. Runs the replica event loop. Blocks
indefinitely; call it from a dedicated FreeRTOS task. The function
dispatches incoming messages by `tag` (1..17) to the appropriate
handler in `src/tbft_replica.c`.

### `Byz_detect_local_id`

```c
int Byz_detect_local_id(const char *config_file);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:287`. Auto-detect the local node ID from the
cluster config file.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `config_file` | Path to the cluster configuration file. |

For ESP-NOW transport, reads the WiFi STA MAC and matches it against
the MAC addresses in the config. For UDP transport, reads the local
STA IP and matches it against the IP addresses in the config. WiFi
(ESP-NOW) or network (UDP) must be initialised and started before
calling this function.

**Return value:** node index (0-based) if found, `-1` if not detected.

### `Byz_reset_stats`

```c
void Byz_reset_stats(void);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:290`. Resets all performance counters.

### `Byz_print_stats`

```c
void Byz_print_stats(void);
```

`include/esp-tinybft.h:293`. Prints current performance statistics to
the ESP-IDF log.

## Module-level singletons

`src/tbft_libbyz.c:41-43` declares three file-static pointers/flags
that hold the live replica or client instance:

| Symbol | Type | Set by | Read by |
|--------|------|--------|---------|
| `s_replica` | `tbft_replica_t *` | `Byz_init_replica` | `Byz_replica_run`, `Byz_modify`, `Byz_modify1` |
| `s_client` | `tbft_node_t *` | `Byz_init_client` | `Byz_send_request`, `Byz_recv_reply`, `Byz_invoke`, `Byz_invoke_with_retry` |
| `s_is_replica` | `bool` | `Byz_init_replica` / `Byz_init_client` | runtime-mode checks in handlers |

A fourth piece of state, the reply collection buffer
(`s_replies[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS]`, `s_reply_count`), is in
`src/tbft_libbyz.c:49-54`. It is indexed by replica id (one slot per
replica) so any quorum count is automatically a count of distinct
senders — a precondition for BFT reply agreement.

There are no public accessors for the singletons. All public state
manipulation goes through the `Byz_*` API.

## Reply collection

`Byz_recv_reply` (`include/esp-tinybft.h:177`) is the public entry point.
The implementation:

1. Resets `s_reply_count` to 0 and marks every `s_replies[i].valid = false`.
2. Enters a poll loop that calls `tbft_node_recv` on the underlying
   transport. Reply messages (tag 13, per the BFT protocol) are matched
   against the in-flight request's digest and `cid`.
3. On the first valid reply from replica `i`, copies the payload into
   `s_replies[i].buf` and increments `s_reply_count`.
4. Returns when `s_reply_count >= f + 1` (the BFT reply agreement
   threshold) and a digest match exists.

The BFT agreement threshold is `f + 1` matching replies from distinct
replicas. With `f = 2` (counter) that is 3 distinct replies; with
`f = 1` (simple_wallet) it is 2. The digest comparison is done in the
library; the caller receives a single canonical reply.

## Lifecycle: init -> run -> shutdown

```c
void app_main(void)
{
    // 1. NVS + SPIFFS + WiFi
    nvs_flash_init();
    esp_vfs_spiffs_register(...);
    wifi_init();

#if CONFIG_EXAMPLE_ROLE_REPLICA
    // 2. Replica role
    int local_id = Byz_detect_local_id("/spiffs/config_espnow.txt");
    char priv[32];
    snprintf(priv, sizeof(priv), "/spiffs/priv%d.der", local_id);
    Byz_init_replica("/spiffs/config_espnow.txt", priv, local_id,
                     app_state, sizeof(app_state),
                     exec_cb, NULL, 0, NULL, 0);
    Byz_replica_run();   // blocks

    // Shutdown: Byz_replica_run() never returns under normal operation.
    // To restart, call esp_restart() or power-cycle.
#else
    // 2. Client role
    int local_id = Byz_detect_local_id("/spiffs/config_espnow.txt");
    char priv[32];
    snprintf(priv, sizeof(priv), "/spiffs/priv%d.der", local_id);
    Byz_init_client("/spiffs/config_espnow.txt", priv, local_id, 0);

    // 3. Client request loop
    while (1) {
        Byz_req req;
        Byz_rep rep;
        Byz_alloc_request(&req, sizeof(my_cmd));
        // ... fill req.contents, set req.size ...
        if (Byz_invoke(&req, &rep, false) == 0) {
            // ... process rep.contents[0..rep.size) ...
        }
        Byz_free_reply(&rep);
        Byz_free_request(&req);
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(1000));
    }
#endif
}
```

**Thread safety** (per `include/esp-tinybft.h:66-68`): `Byz_init_replica`
is NOT thread-safe with respect to `Byz_replica_run`. The caller must
ensure `Byz_replica_run` has exited (the FreeRTOS task has terminated)
before calling `Byz_init_replica` again. In practice, since
`Byz_replica_run` blocks indefinitely, the standard pattern is to call
`esp_restart()` between init cycles.

**Heap ownership:** the `tbft_replica_t` allocated by `Byz_init_replica`
is owned by the library. There is no `Byz_shutdown_replica` public API;
the struct lives until `esp_restart()` or power-cycle.
